results.summary:
Audit of .cache/pip-audit.json against pyproject.toml + uv.lock: 58 vuln records across 18 packages, but ZERO are in haute's [project.dependencies] direct-vulnerable set with a reachable critical path; the headline counts (mlflow x8, pyjwt x11, gitpython x4, pillow x6, flask/werkzeug, cryptography x5) are almost entirely (a) transitive and (b) gated behind the optional `databricks` extra and/or unreachable in haute's actual code paths.

PROVENANCE (from `uv tree --invert`): mlflow, flask, werkzeug, mako, gitpython, cryptography, pyjwt, pyasn1 are ALL pulled ONLY via the `databricks` extra (mlflow / flask-cors / alembic / databricks-sdk / databricks-sql-connector / google-auth). requests + urllib3 are extra-only (+dev via mkdocs-material). pygments, pymdown-extensions, pytest are DEV-ONLY. pillow is transitive via matplotlib (catboost[core]+mlflow) but haute imports NO image code. The only vulnerable packages on the CORE runtime path are: starlette (via fastapi, direct), python-multipart (DIRECT core dep), python-dotenv (DIRECT core dep), idna (via anyio/uvicorn). Of haute's 16 direct [project.dependencies], only python-multipart and python-dotenv appear as vulnerable; both have fixes within the existing upper bounds.

REACHABILITY (from source grep): (1) haute uses mlflow strictly as a CLIENT (set_tracking_uri / log_model / registry / get_experiment_by_name; all `import mlflow` lazy, in deploy/ + modelling/ + routes/mlflow.py + optimiser). It NEVER runs `mlflow server`/`mlflow ui`, so the marquee mlflow server CVEs (PYSEC-2026-93/94 UI XSS + AJAX authz bypass, CVE-2026-0545/2652 basic-auth FastAPI bypass on /ajax-api/3.0/jobs & /v1/traces) are UNREACHABLE, and the flask/werkzeug session+safe_join, mako template-traversal, and gitpython clone/fetch RCE CVEs are all mlflow-server-side and not invoked by a client. (2) pillow: NO matplotlib/PIL import, no Image.open/savefig/FITS/PSD/PDF anywhere in src -> all 6 pillow CVEs UNREACHABLE. (3) starlette IS core (server.py, _local_security.py security middleware) but haute reads request.url.PATH only (never .hostname/.netloc), defends with LocalTrustedHostMiddleware (400 on bad Host), defaults to loopback 127.0.0.1, and its SPA FileResponse enforces is_relative_to(STATIC_DIR) -> the starlette host-spoof/StaticFiles-UNC CVEs are largely neutralised; the urlencoded-limit-bypass (CVE-2026-54283) and multipart DoS are the realest residual, mitigated by loopback default. (4) requests/urllib3 vulns require calling extract_zipped_paths()/streaming/assert_same_host=False directly — not done by haute.

PRIORITISED REMEDIATION:
P1 (real, core, free within bounds): bump python-multipart >=0.0.31 (5 DoS/smuggling CVEs; file-upload routes reachable), starlette via fastapi (limit-bypass + host-spoof) — note fastapi<0.130 pin caps starlette at 0.52.x so the starlette>=1.0 fixes are BLOCKED by the upper bound: this is the one pin-hygiene blocker; raising it needs a fastapi major bump (out of current envelope) so accept-with-mitigation (loopback default) and track. python-dotenv >=1.2.2 (symlink overwrite; local-only).
P2 (defense-in-depth, transitive, regenerate lock): cryptography 46.0.5->latest (buffer overflow CVE-2026-39892 is the only memorable one; reachable via TLS in google-auth), idna >=3.15, pyasn1 >=0.6.3, requests/urllib3 latest — all just `uv lock --upgrade`.
P3 (dev-only, no prod impact): pytest 9.0.3, pygments 2.20.0, pymdown-extensions 10.21.3 — bump the dev pins when convenient.
P4 (databricks-extra only, deferred): mlflow 3.10.0->3.11.x picks up flask/werkzeug/gitpython/mako transitively and closes the client-side CVE-2026-4137 (world-writable tmp) + CVE-2026-10803; do this when revisiting the databricks integration. Requires raising `mlflow<4` is fine (3.11 allowed) and `databricks-sdk<0.89` / `databricks-sql-connector<5` already allow the pyjwt/requests bumps.

NON-ISSUES (unreachable): all 6 pillow CVEs; all mlflow server CVEs (XSS/authz/basic-auth-bypass); flask CVE-2026-27205; werkzeug CVE-2026-27199; mako CVE-2026-44307; all 4 gitpython RCE CVEs; all 11 pyjwt CVEs (databricks-sql-connector internal auth, not haute-invoked); requests CVE-2026-25645 & urllib3 CVEs (APIs not called). LICENSES: dependency set is uniformly permissive (Apache-2.0/MIT/BSD/HPND); no GPL/AGPL-incompatible or commercial license observed -> AGPL-3.0-only project license is satisfied.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-94/CVE-2026-33866 (authz bypass), PYSEC-2026-93/CVE-2026-33865 (stored XSS), PYSEC-2026-195/CVE-2026-10803 (weak hash), CVE-2026-0545 (jobs auth bypass/RCE), CVE-2026-2652 (FastAPI basic-auth bypass), CVE-2026-4137 (world-writable tmp dir RCE), GHSA-7qhf-v65m-g5f3
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: MOSTLY UNREACHABLE. haute imports mlflow lazily as a CLIENT only (set_tracking_uri/log_model/register/get_experiment_by_name in deploy/, modelling/_mlflow_log.py, routes/mlflow.py, optimiser, _mlflow_io). It NEVER starts `mlflow server`/`mlflow ui`, so PYSEC-2026-93/94 (UI XSS + AJAX authz), CVE-2026-0545/2652 (server FastAPI/basic-auth bypass on /ajax-api/3.0/jobs & /v1/traces) cannot be reached. Only CVE-2026-4137 (world-writable model-download tmp dir) and CVE-2026-10803 (weak digest hash) have any client-side surface, and only on a shared/NFS host with a local attacker (Databricks). Only present at all if the databricks extra is installed.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Defer to a databricks-integration pass: bump to mlflow>=3.11.0,<4 (within current `mlflow<4` bound) when next touching the extra; this also pulls fixed flask/werkzeug/gitpython/mako transitively. Not urgent because haute is an mlflow client, not server.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-120/CVE-2026-32597 (crit header not validated), PYSEC-2026-175/CVE-2026-48522 (PyJWKClient SSRF/file://), PYSEC-2026-176/CVE-2026-48523, PYSEC-2026-177/CVE-2026-48524 (unbounded JWKS fetch), PYSEC-2026-178/CVE-2026-48525, PYSEC-2026-179/CVE-2026-48526 (HMAC-with-public-key confusion)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE from haute. Pulled ONLY via databricks-sql-connector (databricks extra). haute has NO `import jwt`; JWT verification is internal to the Databricks SQL connector's OAuth/token handling, not driven by haute-controlled tokens or jku URLs. The SSRF/algorithm-confusion paths need an application that calls jwt.decode/PyJWKClient with attacker-influenced input, which haute does not do.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: No direct action; it rides along when databricks-sql-connector updates. Current `databricks-sql-connector>=4.2.5,<5` already permits a pyjwt>=2.13 resolution on `uv lock --upgrade`. Treat as transitive defense-in-depth, not a haute exposure.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-42215/GHSA-rpm5-65cw-6hj4 (upload_pack kwarg RCE), CVE-2026-42284 (multi_options hooksPath RCE), CVE-2026-44244 (set_value newline -> hooksPath RCE), GHSA-mv93-w799-cj2w (section/option newline injection, incomplete patch)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE from haute. Pulled ONLY via mlflow-skinny (databricks extra). haute has NO `import git`. These are RCE-via-attacker-controlled-kwargs/clone-options/config-values; they are reachable only inside MLflow's own git-based project/model logging when MLflow handles untrusted author_name/repo options — haute does not expose that path.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Closed transitively by the mlflow 3.11.x bump (P4). No standalone action; not a haute-reachable RCE.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-165/CVE-2026-42308 (ImageFont int overflow), CVE-2026-40192 (FITS decompression bomb), CVE-2026-42309 (nested-coords heap overflow), CVE-2026-42310 (PDF infinite loop), CVE-2026-42311 (PSD memory corruption)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE. Pulled via matplotlib (catboost core dep + mlflow). Source grep finds NO matplotlib/PIL import, no Image.open / ImageFont / savefig / FITS / PSD / PDF usage anywhere in src/haute. Every one of these CVEs requires feeding attacker-controlled images/fonts/PDFs/coordinate-lists to Pillow; haute never decodes images.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: None required for security. Optionally allow it to update on `uv lock --upgrade` (matplotlib has no upper bound here). All 6 are non-issues for haute.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-161/CVE-2026-48710 (Host-header path injection -> auth bypass), CVE-2026-54282 (request.url.hostname spoof), CVE-2026-48818 (StaticFiles UNC SSRF on Windows), CVE-2026-48817 (HTTPEndpoint method getattr), CVE-2026-54283 (urlencoded max_fields/max_part_size ignored), CVE-2026-54282
vulnerabilities.fix_version: 1.3.1 (1.0.1 covers the host CVE; 1.1.0 covers StaticFiles/method)
vulnerabilities.dependency_kind: transitive (via fastapi, which is DIRECT core)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: CORE PATH but largely mitigated. starlette underpins haute's FastAPI server + custom security middleware (server.py, _local_security.py). However: (a) the host-spoofing CVEs (48710/54282) only bite code reading request.url.hostname/.netloc — haute reads request.url.PATH only, and runs LocalTrustedHostMiddleware that 400s invalid Host headers; (b) StaticFiles UNC-SSRF (48818) is Windows+UNC-only and haute's /assets mount serves a fixed bundled dir while the SPA fallback enforces file_path.is_relative_to(STATIC_DIR); (c) server defaults to loopback 127.0.0.1. The realistic residual is CVE-2026-54283 (urlencoded body limits silently ignored) -> form-parser DoS, and that requires a non-loopback bind.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: BLOCKED by pin: `fastapi>=0.129,<0.130` caps starlette at 0.52.x, so the starlette>=1.0 fixes cannot be pulled without a fastapi major upgrade (outside the current envelope). Accept-with-mitigation now (loopback default + TrustedHost + path-only URL use); track a coordinated fastapi+starlette bump as a follow-up. Do NOT loosen the fastapi bound ad hoc.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-40347 (preamble/epilogue DoS), CVE-2026-42561 (header-count/size DoS), CVE-2026-53540 (negative Content-Length OOM), CVE-2026-53539 (semicolon O(n^2) DoS), CVE-2026-53538 (semicolon field smuggling)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: CORE & REACHABLE. python-multipart is a DIRECT [project.dependencies] entry (line 36) and haute uses UploadFile/File()/Form() on real upload routes (routes/_save_pipeline.py, _model_scorer.py, modelling/_training_job.py, _mlflow_log.py). The multipart parser processes attacker-supplied request bodies, so the DoS/smuggling paths are reachable — mitigated only by the loopback-by-default bind (attacker must reach the port).
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P1: bump `python-multipart>=0.0.31,<0.1` (well within the existing `<0.1` upper bound). Highest-value DIRECT-dependency fix in this audit; closes all 5 CVEs at once.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-28684/GHSA-mf9w-mj56-hr94 (set_key/unset_key follow symlinks -> arbitrary file overwrite)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: CORE but low. DIRECT dep (line 37); haute uses dotenv via load_dotenv (deploy/_config.py) which READS env files, not the vulnerable set_key/unset_key WRITE path. Exploit needs a local attacker planting a symlink at the .env path plus a cross-device temp rename, and haute does not call set_key. Local-only, write-path not exercised.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P1 (cheap): bump `python-dotenv>=1.2.2,<2` (within `<2` bound). Trivial and removes the symlink-overwrite primitive even though haute uses the read path.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-35/CVE-2026-34073 (name-constraint bypass), PYSEC-2026-36/CVE-2026-39892 (non-contiguous buffer overflow in Hash.update), GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf (bundled OpenSSL advisory)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: LOW / extra-only. Pulled via mlflow + google-auth/databricks-sdk (databricks extra). haute has NO `import cryptography`. CVE-2026-39892 (buffer overflow) needs passing a non-contiguous buffer to Hash.update — not done by haute. The name-constraint bypass needs an uncommon X.509 topology (authors rate it medium-low). Bundled-OpenSSL item only matters for the PyPI wheel TLS used by databricks-sdk/google-auth.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P2: include in `uv lock --upgrade` to reach >=46.0.7 (or 48.x for the OpenSSL fix). Only relevant when the databricks extra is installed; defense-in-depth for the TLS stack.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-215/CVE-2026-45409 (idna.encode DoS on crafted long input, incomplete CVE-2024-3651 fix)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: LOW. Reaches the core path via anyio (fastapi->starlette, uvicorn, watchfiles) and httpx/requests. The DoS needs an arbitrarily large (>253 char) domain string passed to idna.encode(); haute does not feed user-controlled hostnames to idna directly. Triggered only by inputs that would not occur in normal hostname handling.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P2: `uv lock --upgrade` to idna>=3.15 (no upper bound constrains it). Low urgency.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-30922/GHSA-jr27-m4p2-rc6r (uncontrolled recursion -> DoS on nested ASN.1)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE in practice. Pulled via pyasn1-modules/rsa -> google-auth -> databricks-sdk (databricks extra). haute does not parse untrusted ASN.1/DER; pyasn1 is used internally by google-auth for service-account key parsing of trusted credentials, not attacker data.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P2: bump on `uv lock --upgrade` to >=0.6.3. Defense-in-depth; only present with the databricks extra.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-25645/GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2 (extract_zipped_paths predictable temp filename)
vulnerabilities.dependency_kind: transitive (extra: databricks; also dev via mkdocs-material)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE. The advisory states standard requests usage is NOT affected; only direct callers of requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths() are. haute has NO `import requests` and never calls that helper. Pulled via databricks-sdk/sql-connector/docker/mlflow (extra) and mkdocs-material (dev).
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P2/none: let it update on `uv lock --upgrade`. Non-issue for haute (helper not called).

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: PYSEC-2026-142/CVE-2026-44432 (streaming over-decompression DoS), PYSEC-2026-141/CVE-2026-44431 (cross-origin redirect leaks auth headers via ProxyManager + assert_same_host=False)
vulnerabilities.dependency_kind: transitive (extra: databricks; also dev via mkdocs-material)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: LOW/UNREACHABLE. haute has NO `import urllib3`. CVE-2026-44431 requires the low-level ProxyManager API with assert_same_host=False; CVE-2026-44432 affects the streaming API with attacker-controlled Content-Encoding. These are used (if at all) internally by requests/databricks-sdk/docker against trusted Databricks/registry endpoints, not haute-driven untrusted servers.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P2: `uv lock --upgrade` to urllib3>=2.7.0. Defense-in-depth for the HTTP stack.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-27205/GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 (missing Vary: Cookie on `in` session access -> cache leak)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE. Pulled ONLY via flask-cors -> mlflow (databricks extra). Flask is the MLflow tracking-server web framework; haute runs FastAPI, not Flask, and does not start the mlflow server. The session-caching leak requires a Flask app behind a caching proxy — not haute.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Closed by mlflow 3.11.x bump (P4). No haute action; non-issue.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-27199/GHSA-29vq-49wr-vm6x (safe_join allows Windows device names in multi-segment paths -> send_from_directory hangs)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE. Pulled via flask -> flask-cors -> mlflow (databricks extra). werkzeug.safe_join/send_from_directory is exercised by the MLflow Flask server's artifact serving, not by haute (which serves static files through starlette/FastAPI with its own is_relative_to guard).
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Closed by mlflow 3.11.x bump (P4). No haute action; non-issue.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-44307/GHSA-2h4p-vjrc-8xpq (Windows backslash traversal in TemplateLookup.get_template)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: UNREACHABLE. Pulled via alembic -> mlflow (databricks extra). mako is used by alembic for DB migration templates inside MLflow; haute does not pass user-controlled template names to mako TemplateLookup.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Closed by mlflow/alembic update under the 3.11.x bump (P4). No haute action; non-issue.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-4539/GHSA-5239-wwwm-4pmq (ReDoS in AdlLexer, local access)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: DEV-ONLY, not shipped. Pulled via mkdocs-material (docs build) and pytest (test output highlighting). The ReDoS needs feeding crafted ADL source to the Pygments ADL lexer during a local docs/test run; not in any haute runtime path.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P3: bump on next dev-tooling refresh (no pin pins pygments directly; it follows mkdocs-material/pytest). Non-issue for production.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2026-46338/GHSA-62q4-447f-wv8h (snippets prefix-match path traversal to sibling dirs)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: DEV-ONLY, not shipped. Pulled via mkdocs-material / mkdocstrings (docs build). Affects mkdocs snippet inclusion at docs-build time only; never in the haute package.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P3: update with the docs toolchain. Non-issue for production.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: CVE-2025-71176/GHSA-6w46-j5rx-g56g (predictable /tmp/pytest-of-<user> dir, local DoS/priv-esc on UNIX)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: DEV-ONLY, not shipped. Pinned `pytest==9.0.2` in dependency-groups.dev. Local multi-user-host issue during test runs only; Windows-dev and CI runners are not meaningfully exposed.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: P3: bump the pin to `pytest==9.0.3`. Trivial; non-issue for production.

hygiene_findings.detail: `fastapi>=0.129.0,<0.130` transitively caps starlette at 0.52.x. The starlette CVE fixes that matter (host-spoof, StaticFiles, urlencoded limit bypass) land in starlette>=1.0.1/1.1.0/1.3.1, which fastapi 0.129 does not allow. So the single most security-relevant upper bound in pyproject is currently blocking the starlette patches.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Do NOT widen the fastapi bound ad hoc (starlette 1.x is a breaking change for fastapi). Plan a coordinated bump to a fastapi release that depends on starlette>=1.3 as a follow-up; until then rely on haute's existing mitigations (loopback default bind, LocalTrustedHostMiddleware Host validation, request.url.path-only usage, is_relative_to static guard). Add a regression test asserting the server rejects spoofed Host headers and that form-field limits are enforced for urlencoded bodies (the CVE-2026-54283 gap) so a future starlette bump is verified.

hygiene_findings.detail: Two DIRECT core deps ship vulnerable floors that have free in-range fixes: `python-multipart>=0.0.22,<0.1` (fix 0.0.31 is < 0.1) and `python-dotenv>=1.2.1,<2` (fix 1.2.2 is < 2). The upper bounds are fine; only the resolved/lower versions are stale.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Raise the lower pins to `python-multipart>=0.0.31,<0.1` and `python-dotenv>=1.2.2,<2` (or just `uv lock --upgrade-package python-multipart --upgrade-package python-dotenv`). These are the only DIRECT-dependency security fixes and both are zero-risk within existing bounds.

hygiene_findings.detail: cryptography (46.0.7), idna (3.15), pyasn1 (0.6.3), requests (2.33.0), urllib3 (2.7.0) all have fixes with NO blocking upper bound in pyproject (they are unpinned transitives) but the lock is pinned to older versions.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Run `uv lock --upgrade` to refresh the transitive graph, then re-run pip-audit to confirm the count drops. Low risk; defense-in-depth. Most of these only ship under the databricks extra anyway.

hygiene_findings.detail: The entire mlflow/databricks stack (mlflow x8, pyjwt x11, gitpython x4, flask, werkzeug, mako, cryptography x5, pyasn1, plus heavy transitives: alembic, docker, graphene/graphql, sqlalchemy via alembic, gunicorn-free flask server) is pulled ONLY by the optional `databricks` extra. It is, however, force-installed in dependency-groups.dev via `haute[databricks]`, so every developer/CI env resolves the full vulnerable set even though production installs without the extra are clean.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Keep mlflow/databricks strictly optional (good current design). Consider a CI matrix split: run the default security audit against the CORE dependency set (no extra) to reflect the real shipped attack surface, and a separate informational audit with the databricks extra. This makes the audit count honest about what end users actually install (core: only starlette/python-multipart/python-dotenv/idna are vulnerable).

hygiene_findings.detail: pillow (12MB+, 6 CVEs) and the matplotlib stack reach the CORE install via catboost->matplotlib, but haute imports NO matplotlib/PIL and never plots or decodes images. matplotlib is also pulled by mlflow. It is effectively dead weight on the core runtime that nonetheless contributes 6 CVEs to the audit headline.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Confirm catboost cannot be installed without matplotlib (it is a hard dep of catboost, so it cannot be trimmed without dropping catboost). Since the image code is unreachable, treat all pillow CVEs as non-issues but document the rationale so future audits don't re-triage them. No action needed beyond letting pillow float to 12.2.0 on lock refresh.

hygiene_findings.detail: AGPL-3.0-only project. Reviewed the resolved dependency set: fastapi/starlette/pydantic/uvicorn/click/orjson/pillow (MIT/HPND), polars (MIT), catboost/mlflow/databricks-sdk/databricks-sql-connector/cryptography/protobuf (Apache-2.0), gitpython/joblib/numpy/prettytable/lz4/pyasn1 (BSD), pyjwt (MIT). No GPL-2.0-only (incompatible-with-AGPLv3-as-licensee-imposed), no commercial/proprietary, and no SSPL/BUSL packages observed in the lock.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: No license conflict for distribution under AGPL-3.0-only: all dependencies are permissive (MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0/HPND) which AGPLv3 may incorporate. Note Apache-2.0 is one-way compatible INTO (A)GPLv3 (fine here). Keep an eye that no future dep introduces GPL/AGPL-incompatible terms; a periodic `pip-licenses`/`uv`-based license scan in CI would make this a guardrail rather than a manual check.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (CVE pending; CWE-862)
vulnerabilities.fix_version: 4.1.9 (npm reports fix under @vitest/coverage-v8 4.1.9; bump vitest itself to >=4.1.0, recommend 4.1.9; NON-major)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: NOT shipped to browser. CVE requires the Vitest UI server to be listening (vitest --ui / @vitest/ui). @vitest/ui is NOT installed (absent from package-lock) and the test script is `vitest run` (headless). In practice UNREACHABLE, but installed version 4.0.18 is inside the affected range >=4.0.0 <4.1.0, so it is flagged. Treat as latent: any contributor running `vitest --ui` after installing the UI would be exposed (arbitrary file read+exec, CVSS 9.8).
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Bump devDependency vitest 4.0.18 -> 4.1.9 (clean minor). Do together with @vitest/coverage-v8 so versions stay in lockstep. No code changes expected.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp (inherited via vitest; CWE-862)
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: NOT shipped to browser. Only flagged because it depends on the vulnerable vitest. No independent vulnerable code path; coverage provider runs in the `vitest run --coverage` headless flow. Same UNREACHABLE-UI reasoning as vitest.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Bump @vitest/coverage-v8 4.0.18 -> 4.1.9 in lockstep with vitest. This single bump pair clears BOTH 'critical' findings.

vulnerabilities.vuln_ids: HIGH: GHSA-p9ff-h696-f583 (arbitrary file read via dev-server WebSocket), GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff (server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alt paths); GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3 is reported high in some feeds (launch-editor NTLMv2 hash disclosure, bundled). MODERATE: GHSA-93m4-6634-74q7, GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9. LOW: GHSA-g4jq-h2w9-997c, GHSA-jqfw-vq24-v9c3 (8 advisories total).
vulnerabilities.current_note: audit json reports cvss score 0 for these entries (truncated feed), but the GHSA severities are high/moderate/low as listed
vulnerabilities.dependency_kind: direct dev (devDependencies). NOTE: launch-editor is NOT a separate node in the lock file; that advisory is surfaced through the vite range and is fixed by the same vite bump.
vulnerabilities.runtime_exposure: NOT shipped to browser (vite is the build tool / dev server). All high CVEs require an ACTIVELY RUNNING dev server (`vite` / `vite preview`) reachable by an attacker. Local dev server has no `server.host` override in vite.config.ts so it binds localhost only. E2E does NOT use `vite dev` (playwright webServer runs `uv run python scripts/run_frontend_e2e_server.py`). Production build output is static files in ../src/haute/static and contains none of this code. So exposure is limited to a developer running the dev server on an untrusted network; the WebSocket file-read (GHSA-p9ff-h696-f583) is the most serious of these.
vulnerabilities.recommended_action: Bump devDependency vite 6.3.5 -> 6.4.3 (clean minor within the v6 line). This also pulls a postcss >=8.5.10 subtree, clearing the postcss moderate finding transitively, and removes the launch-editor advisory. Verify build still emits to ../src/haute/static.

hygiene_findings.detail: All entries in dependencies and devDependencies use EXACT pins (no ^ or ~), e.g. react 19.2.4, vite 6.3.5, vitest 4.0.18. This is good supply-chain hygiene (reproducible installs) and is backed by package-lock.json + a committed bun.lock. The float only exists in transitive ranges inside the lockfile.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Keep exact pins. When applying the security bumps, update BOTH the exact pin in package.json AND regenerate package-lock.json (and bun.lock) so the two lockfiles stay consistent.

hygiene_findings.detail: Both frontend/package-lock.json (npm; CI uses `npm ci`) and frontend/bun.lock (bun) are committed. The audit and CI are npm-based. Divergence between the two could mean a `bun install` resolves different transitive versions than CI audits.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: Treat package-lock.json as the source of truth for CI/audit. After security bumps, regenerate bun.lock in the same change (or document that bun is not the supported install path) to avoid drift between the two resolved trees.

hygiene_findings.detail: Checked the suspicious-looking devDeps. @babel/parser, @babel/traverse, @babel/types (pinned 7.29.0) are NOT unused: they are imported by frontend/scripts/check-ui-dependencies.mjs and the AST architecture-guard tests (src/__tests__/hover/previewPanelsHover.test.tsx, editorsHover.test.tsx). elkjs 0.11.0 is used by src/utils/layout.ts (graph auto-layout) and ships to the browser legitimately. lucide-react is used across ~30 components. No dead production or dev dependency identified.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: No removal needed. (If desired, run `npx depcheck` / `knip` as a periodic CI hygiene gate, but current manifest is clean.)

hygiene_findings.detail: Heaviest shipped deps are the @codemirror/* family (8 packages: autocomplete/commands/lang-python/language/lint/search/state/view) plus @lezer grammars, @xyflow/react 12.10.0 (React Flow), elkjs 0.11.0 (ELK layout engine, large WASM/JS), and react/react-dom 19. The vite config already code-splits these into dedicated manual chunks (vendor-react, vendor-layout=elkjs, vendor-codemirror, vendor-ui=lucide-react), and the repo has check-bundle-size.mjs + analyze-bundle-sourcemaps.mjs guards. elkjs is the single largest non-React bundle contributor.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: No action required for security. For bundle weight, the existing manualChunks + check:bundle gate is the right control; keep elkjs and codemirror lazy/chunked. None of these shipped deps have advisories.

hygiene_findings.detail: Project is AGPL-3.0. Every package in the affected (vulnerable) paths is MIT-licensed (@babel/core MIT, js-yaml MIT, postcss MIT, undici MIT, vite MIT, vitest MIT, jsdom MIT). The shipped dependency set (react, @xyflow/react, @codemirror/*, elkjs, lucide-react, zustand, tailwindcss) is MIT/ISC/permissive. No copyleft (GPL/AGPL) or unknown-license dependency that would conflict with redistribution.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: No license conflict. (Optional: add an automated license-allowlist check in CI to keep it that way.)

hygiene_findings.detail: All 7 vulnerabilities are dev/build-only (every affected node is marked `"dev": true` in the lockfile: 0 production deps affected — metadata shows prod=74 with no vulnerable prod node). All 7 fixes are NON-major (clean minor/patch bumps: vitest/coverage-v8 -> 4.1.9, vite -> 6.4.3, undici -> >=7.28.0, postcss -> >=8.5.10, js-yaml -> >4.1.1, @babel/core -> >7.29.0). No breaking major upgrade is required to remediate any finding. Direct deps (react 19, vite 6, vitest 4, eslint 9, typescript 5.9) are on current majors; nothing is dangerously stale.
hygiene_findings.recommendation: No major-version migration needed. Apply the in-range bumps; the shipped runtime bundle requires no changes at all.

results.summary:
7 advisories (2 critical, 2 high, 2 moderate, 1 low), and the single most important fact is that ALL 7 are dev/build-only: every affected node in package-lock.json is marked `"dev": true`, and ZERO production/shipped-to-browser packages are vulnerable. The browser bundle (react/react-dom 19.2.4, @xyflow/react 12.10.0, @codemirror/* family, elkjs 0.11.0, lucide-react, zustand 5, tailwindcss 4) has no advisories. Equally important: every fix is a NON-major (clean minor/patch) bump — no breaking upgrade is required.

Prioritised remediation order (one PR, two effective bumps clear 4 of 7 findings):
1. FIRST — Bump vite 6.3.5 -> 6.4.3 (direct dev). Clears the vite HIGH cluster (incl. dev-server WebSocket arbitrary file read GHSA-p9ff-h696-f583 and server.fs.deny bypass GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff and the bundled launch-editor advisory) AND transitively pulls postcss >=8.5.10, clearing the postcss moderate. Highest real-world severity because the vite dev server is the only component an attacker could plausibly reach (though only when a dev runs `vite`/`vite preview` on an untrusted network; CI E2E does NOT use the vite dev server).
2. SECOND — Bump vitest 4.0.18 -> 4.1.9 AND @vitest/coverage-v8 4.0.18 -> 4.1.9 in lockstep (both direct dev). Clears BOTH 'critical' findings in one pair. Despite the 9.8 score, the critical CVE (GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp) requires the Vitest UI server, which is NOT installed (@vitest/ui absent) and never started (`vitest run` is headless) — so it is effectively UNREACHABLE today; fix it to remove the latent footgun and the audit noise.
3. THIRD (low urgency, transitive hygiene) — Run `npm update undici js-yaml @babel/core` (or `npm audit fix`) to advance undici -> >=7.28.0 (HIGH by score but only loaded by jsdom as the test DOM environment — no real network/WS/SOCKS5 client, so non-reachable), js-yaml -> patched 4.x (eslint config parsing only), and @babel/core -> patched 7.x (build-time JSX transform only, low). Regenerate both package-lock.json and bun.lock to keep the dual lockfiles consistent.

CVEs that are effectively NON-ISSUES because the vulnerable path is unreachable in this project (fix for hygiene/CI-cleanliness, not because of live risk): the vitest critical (no UI server), the undici high cluster (jsdom test-only, not used as an HTTP/WS client), postcss XSS (build-time, first-party CSS only), js-yaml DoS (first-party eslint config only), @babel/core file-read (first-party source only). The genuinely-attacker-facing residual is the vite dev-server file-read, and even that only when a developer exposes the dev server on a hostile network. Net: cosmetically 2 critical + 2 high, but real runtime risk to the deployed product is effectively zero; remediation is a handful of in-range bumps with no impact on the shipped bundle.
